subject.title: cron: ghost runs recorded as ok when gateway is down (durationMs < 50ms)

question: Should the fix be a default-on persisted warning with config/protocol/UI surface, a narrower log-only warning, or a behavior-changing skipped/error outcome for these fast handoffs?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the open candidate changes operator configuration and generated protocol/run-log shape, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Refresh the linked warning PR
options.body: Resolve conflicts, remove unrelated drift, and land the warning with maintainer-approved config/protocol behavior.

options.title: Replace with a narrower diagnostic
options.body: Close or pause the current branch and land a smaller log-only or run-log-only warning if the config/protocol surface is too broad.

options.title: Change run status semantics
options.body: Treat these handoffs as skipped or error when delivery cannot be proven, accepting a larger behavior change with upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Refresh the linked warning PR
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, remove unrelated drift, and land the warning with maintainer-approved config/protocol behavior.
